These **specifications** were not part of the original offer but were **added** by the appellee in their acceptance notice. Although the court ultimately ruled in favor of Fairmount, the crux of the issue was whether the **specifications** constituted an addition or an implied part of the offer. The court found that the specifications were *part of the trade* understanding and formed the foundation of the contract.
